question: The Indian Vice President is elected by an electoral college comprising members of _______________.

options.text: Rajya Sabha, Lok Sabha and State Legislative Council
Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Assembly

solution:
The correct answer is __**both the houses of Parliament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Vice President of India is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both houses of Parliament: the Rajya Sabha and the Lok Sabha.
 
• The election is conducted in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.
 
• The Vice President serves a term of five years but can be re-elected.
 
• To be eligible for the position of Vice President, a candidate must be a citizen of India, at least 35 years old, and qualified to be a member of the Rajya Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Electoral College**

 
 
• An electoral college is a body of electors chosen or appointed by a larger group, in this case, members of both houses of Parliament in India.
 
• The members of the electoral college vote to elect the Vice President of India.
 
 
 
• **Proportional Representation**
 
 
• Proportional representation is a voting system aimed at achieving a close match between the percentage of votes and the percentage of seats obtained by each party or group of candidates.
 
• This system ensures that minority groups have a chance of representation in the elected body.
 
 
 
• **Single Transferable Vote**
 
 
• The single transferable vote (STV) is a voting system designed to achieve proportional representation through ranked voting in multi-seat organizations or constituencies.
 
• Under STV, voters rank candidates in order of preference, and candidates are elected sequentially based on those preferences.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Vice President**
 
 
• The Vice President of India is the second-highest constitutional office in the country, after the President.
 
• The Vice President acts as the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha (Council of States).
 
• In the absence of the President, the Vice President assumes the duties and responsibilities of the President.
